Diversity of Cells
Cells, both among and within, organisms are very diverse:
Vary in shape, size, internal organization, function
Varying function of cells a product of their different structures
Can be simpleor complexdepending on function
Structure has evolvedto allow most effective functionality
explanation: Cells, both among and within organisms, exhibit immense diversity. They vary significantly in their shape, size, internal organization, and function. The varying function of cells is directly a product of their different structures; structure has evolved over time to allow the most effective functionality, whether simple or complex depending on the cell's function.

questions.q: Which of the following is the primary reason why different cell types have different functions?
opts: They vary in their structures, which have evolved for specific functions.
They belong to different taxonomic kingdoms.
They are formed in different parts of the organism.
questions.exp: The slide states that the varying function of cells is a product of their different structures, which evolved to allow most effective functionality.
